place.source_title: Valley Grove Churches, Old Church, County Road 29

brief: Norwegian Lutheran country church of 1862 on a hilltop crossroads: a plain rectangular nave of coursed limestone with round-arched windows, a gable-front entrance with a small white frame belfry cupola on the ridge, standing in a fenced churchyard beside its taller white-painted 1894 frame successor, entered through an iron gateway arch lettered VALLEY GROVE.

facade.notes: Valley Grove (Nerstrand MN): the 1862 old church -- a plain coursed-limestone nave with a small belfry on the ridge -- and the white frame 1894 church with a spire beside it, on a hilltop behind a wire farm gate under an iron 'Valley Grove' arch; a Norwegian Lutheran congregation's two churches and cemetery

why.note: a church is a long nave pointed at the street (or east) with a tower or belfry marking the entrance
immigrant country churches stood on a donated hilltop acre at a crossroads, with the cemetery around them
